title: Set up a product dashboard
summary: A dashboard puts the numbers that matter in one place, so the team can see how the product is doing every week without waiting for reports.

beginner: Put your main success metric at the top, with its target.
Add the supporting metrics and guardrails under it.
Show trends over time, not just today's number, and mark key releases.
Keep it to one screen. If it needs scrolling, it has too much on it.
Review it with the team every week and note what changed and why.
intermediate: Build a dashboard around the primary metric, inputs and guardrails.
Show trends, targets and release markers.
Add breakdowns for key user groups.
Use it in a weekly team review.
experienced: Link the dashboard to the north star metric and its input metrics.
Use a framework such as HEART to cover user experience, not just business numbers.
Add automatic alerts for big changes.
Make the dashboard the basis of regular business reviews.

canDelegateTo.task: Build the dashboard and check the numbers are right
Help make the dashboard clear and readable

toolExamples.looker: Build the dashboard on shared metric definitions so everyone sees the same numbers.
toolExamples.power-bi: Create a one-page report with targets and trend lines.
toolExamples.amplitude: Build a dashboard of saved charts and share it with the team.
toolExamples.ga4: Use a custom report collection for the main journeys.

definitionOfDone: Dashboard shows primary metric, supporting metrics and guardrails
pitfalls: Looking at it once and forgetting it

leaderView.good: Teams look at a small set of meaningful numbers every week and act on them.
ask: What does the dashboard tell us this week, and what are we doing about it?
How does it link to our north star metric?
signs: Dashboards exist but no one looks at them.

sources.title: Measuring the user experience on a large scale: the HEART framework (Google Research)
